subject: Chemistry
title: Lithium: From Rocks to Batteries
description: One-minute skill: Lithium: From Rocks to Batteries.

hook.text: Lithium is the lightest metal on Earth. It floats on water—right before it reacts and catches fire.

buildup.text: Discovered in 1817 in a mineral from a Swedish mine, its name comes from 'lithos'—Greek for stone.

discovery.text: Lithium's tiny size lets its ions move easily through materials, making it perfect for rechargeable batteries.

twist.text: It also treats bipolar disorder. Nobody fully understands why it stabilizes mood, but it works.

climax.text: Lithium powers phones, laptops, and electric cars. Demand has made it 'white gold.'

punchline.text: A metal from stone that powers the modern world.

quiz.question: What makes lithium ideal for rechargeable batteries?
options: Its tiny ions move easily through materials

details.summary: Lithium, discovered in 1817 by Johan August Arfwedson in the mineral petalite, is the lightest metal and the third element on the periodic table..
details.whyItMatters: Lithium-ion batteries power smartphones, laptops, electric vehicles, and grid energy storage. Control of lithium reserves has become a major geopolitical issue as the world transitions from fossil fuels.
takeaways: Lithium is the lightest metal, with just three protons and extremely low density
It was used in psychiatric medicine for bipolar disorder before its tech applications
Lithium-ion batteries now underpin the global transition to electric transportation

faq.question: Why is lithium uniquely suited for rechargeable battery technology?
faq.answer: Lithium is the lightest metal, giving batteries high energy density per kilogram. Its atoms easily release and accept electrons, enabling efficient charge-discharge cycles. Lithium ions are small enough to move quickly through electrode materials, allowing fast charging..

faq.question: Where does most of the world's lithium come from?
faq.answer: About 60% of known lithium reserves are in the Lithium Triangle of South America, spanning Chile, Bolivia, and Argentina, where lithium is extracted from underground brine pools. Australia is the largest producer from hard-rock spodumene mining..
